# Modern Web Guidance (Source) This repo is the source repository for [GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance) and includes the code and documentation for authoring, calibrating, and evaluating its contents. [**Modern Web Guidance**](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/modern-web-guidance) is a set of skills that embed web platform expertise, best practices, and browser compatibility data directly into your coding agents. It helps to steer your coding agents away from legacy patterns, and instead toward solutions that harness the power and capabilities of the modern web platform. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) and [GOVERNANCE.md](./GOVERNANCE.md) for how we work on the project and orientation of the codebase. --- *Stewarded by the Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox, and MDN teams, alongside the web development community.* [Documentation](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/modern-web-guidance) · [Eval Dashboard](https://googlechrome.github.io/modern-web-guidance-src/) · [Source Code](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src) · [Report an Issue](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src/issues) ## Quickstart ```shell npx modern-web-guidance@latest install ``` This command runs an interactive wizard to install Modern Web Guidance. See [Alternative Installation Methods](#-alternative-installation-methods) below. #### Try it out (without installing) ```shell # Search for relevant guides npx modern-web-guidance@latest search "animate a dialog modal backdrop" # Retrieve a guide by ID npx modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "animate-to-from-top-layer" # Scan a codebase for legacy patterns to modernize npx modern-web-guidance@latest legacy-scan . ``` ## Why? Coding agents often default to older patterns because LLM training data contains vast amounts of legacy code. This often leads them to generate bloated JavaScript for tasks that now have native, high-performance web platform solutions. Even if a model knows an API exists, it often lacks the density of real-world, modern implementation patterns required for production-ready code. **Modern Web Guidance bridges this gap.** Our skill's CLI returns targeted, expert-curated guidelines directly into your agent's context window, focusing on: * **Modern Browser APIs**: Helping models correctly structure APIs they frequently misuse. * **Performance & Accessibility**: Preferring platform-level APIs that can be optimized by the browser and include built-in accessibility affordances. * **Responsible Fallbacks**: Guiding models to use sensible, lightweight fallbacks instead of heavy polyfills or legacy libraries. ## What's Included? We cover the past several years of the web platform's new features, all the way up to the cutting edge. The guides are **designed to be token-efficient**; we run evals enabling us to prune lowest-common-denominator content that models already know. ### Core Disciplines

🎨 User Experience

Smooth visual states (View Transitions, entry/exit animations, parallax scroll, CSS scrollbar-color).

📐 CSS Layout

Modern layout systems (container queries, subgrid, modern color spaces like oklch, text-wrap tuning, and line-height trimming).

⚡ Performance

Speed optimizations (instant preloading, Interaction to Next Paint (INP) diagnostics, and scheduling tasks via scheduler.yield).

📝 Forms & UI

Native components (Anchor Positioning for tooltips, Popover API, dialogs, :user-invalid validation, and auto-sizing fields).

♿ Accessibility

Important considerations (screen reader and keyboard operability, content navigation and discoverability).

🤖 Built-in AI

Local client models (native translation, summarization, and language detection APIs).
_View an example:_ [the `navigation-drawer` guide](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance/blob/main/skills/modern-web-guidance/guides/ui-components/navigation-drawer.md). #### The full list

**[optimize-script-priority](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance/blob/main/skills/modern-web-guidance/guides/performance/optimize-script-priority.md)**: Optimize the loading priority of scripts by boosting critical asynchronous scripts and deprioritizing non-essential or late-body scripts to improve sequencing and reduce delays. - **[out-of-order-html-streaming](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance/blob/main/skills/modern-web-guidance/guides/performance/out-of-order-html-streaming.md)**: Declaratively update a page with content streamed later into the same HTML document or via imperative JavaScript APIs. - ### Safe Adoption of Modern Features * **Progressive Enhancement & Nuanced Fallbacks**: We distinguish between purely additive enhancements (like speculative preloading) which are safe to let older browsers silently ignore, and critical behaviors (like dialog controls or network beacons) where we write highly considered, low-overhead fallbacks. * **Responsible Fallbacks**: We prioritize lightweight, case-specific custom fallbacks (<50 LOC) or conditionally-loaded polyfills instead of heavy third-party bundles. * **Gotchas & Quirks**: We document hidden platform limitations, such as the 64KB payload quota for `fetchLater()` or macOS-specific scrollbar behaviors. * **Baseline-Aware Integration**: We leverage real-time compatibility data from the **Baseline** project so agents dynamically adapt to current browser support. * **Origin Trial & Volatile Feature Gates**: Guides covering experimental **Origin Trial** APIs or **volatile features** (single-engine features shipped within the last 3 months or still stabilizing) remain discoverable via `search`, but are gated on `retrieve` so agents do not adopt unstable APIs without explicit developer consent. ### Project Configuration (`.mwgrc`) Configure Origin Trial and volatile feature opt-ins for a repository with an optional `.mwgrc` JSON file in your project root (or `~/.mwgrc` as a user-level fallback), which you can commit to share across your team: | CLI Command | `.mwgrc` Key | Effect | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `npx modern-web-guidance@latest set-allow-origin-trials` | `"allowOriginTrials": true` | Unlocks guides for experimental Origin Trial APIs. | | `npx modern-web-guidance@latest set-allow-volatile-features` | `"allowVolatileFeatures": true` | Unlocks guides for volatile single-engine features. | ## How It Works 1. **Activation**: The coding agent activates the `modern-web-guidance` skill because of a relevant task. The agent is instructed to use the `modern-web-guidance` CLI for web platform queries. 2. **Local Semantic Search**: The agent runs `modern-web-guidance search ""`. The tool matches the query to the best guide using an offline, zero-dependency embedding model and BM25 search engine (no network calls, no API keys). 3. **Guide Fetch**: The agent retrieves the guide via `modern-web-guidance retrieve `, inserting targeted code patterns, gotchas, and fallbacks directly into its context window. > [!TIP] > Note: We use `npx` to ensure the content doesn't go stale, but the CLI works offline, completely private and local. > The npm package is self-contained, with no extra dependencies to ensure both low-latency and supply-chain security. ## Alternative Installation Methods
Vercel Skills CLI (aka npx skills) ```shell npx skills add GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance ```
GitHub CLI ```shell gh skill install GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance ```
Google Antigravity ```shell agy plugin install https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance ```
GitHub Copilot CLI ```shell /plugin marketplace add GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance /plugin install modern-web-guidance@googlechrome ```
Claude Code Plugin ```shell /plugin marketplace add GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance /plugin install modern-web-guidance@googlechrome /plugin # Select GoogleChrome marketplace, press enter, enable AutoUpdate /reload-plugins ```
Grok Build CLI ```shell grok plugin install https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance --trust ```
Kimi Code ```shell /plugins install https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance ```
OpenAI Codex ```shell codex plugin marketplace add GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance codex plugin add modern-web-guidance@googlechrome ```
## Updating If you installed the skill using `npx modern-web-guidance@latest install`, you can update with: `npx modern-web-guidance@latest update`.
Claude Code (if installed via claude-plugins-official) Anthropic stopped updating third-party plugins in their built-in `claude-plugins-official` marketplace on Oct 12, stranding installs at `v0.0.194` ([details](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src/issues/3533)). Switch to the `googlechrome` marketplace to get updates: ```shell /plugin uninstall modern-web-guidance@claude-plugins-official /plugin marketplace add GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance /plugin install modern-web-guidance@googlechrome /plugin # Select GoogleChrome marketplace, press enter, enable AutoUpdate /reload-plugins ```
Otherwise, consult your agent's documentation for updating plugins and skills. ## Evals to prove this works well We developed a robust eval harness to ensure that the content is **empirically proven and continuously calibrated** so AI agents write better code. We run automated evaluations using a closed-loop validation pipeline: ``` [ Expert-authored guidance and demo ] │ ▼ [ Target generation ] ──> Tasks on real webapps, Golden solutions, Playwright graders │ ▼ [ Calibration loop ] ───> Runs Grader on Golden Solutions (Must Pass 100%) │ Runs Grader on Unmodified Base App (Must Fail 100%) ▼ [ E2E agent evals ] ────> Runs coding agents in guided vs. unguided modes Compares pass rates and accessibility w/ and w/o the skill ``` 1. **Simulated Developer Tasks**: We define realistic developer prompts against full base applications (`daily-grind`, `devtools-times`) that mimic real-world requests (e.g., "make my images load faster"). Prompts avoid naming APIs or features, testing whether the agent can naturally discover and apply the right guides. 2. **Static & Browser-Based Checks**: Playwright graders verify that each implementation requirement was followed—checking source patterns, computed styles, runtime DOM behaviors, and accessibility states. 3. **Self-Healing Calibration**: Graders are calibrated against multi-agent (Claude/Codex/AGY) golden solutions (100% pass target) and an unmodified baseline application (0% pass target). 4. **E2E Testing**: We measure coding agent performance on real tasks with and without guidance. The _opportunity_ (100% - unguided pass rate) and _uplift_ (guided - unguided pass rate) are key: if models already succeed without guidance, we prune redundant advice; where agents struggle, we refine guides to maximize uplift. ### Recent eval results snapshot Explore full per-agent and per-guide breakdowns on the **[Eval Dashboard](https://googlechrome.github.io/modern-web-guidance-src/)**. | Date | Agent + Model | Tasks / Checks | Unguided → Guided (Uplift) | | :--- | :--- | :---: | :---: | | Nov 8 | antigravity_cli (gemini-4-argon) | 214 / 1673 | 58% → 94% (**+36pp**) | | Nov 8 | codex_cli (gpt-6.1-sol) | 215 / 1795 | 54% → 82% (**+28pp**) | | Nov 8 | claude_code (opus-5-5) | 215 / 1801 | 57% → 88% (**+31pp**) | | Nov 6 | codex_cli (gpt-6.1-sol) | 212 / 1773 | 53% → 86% (**+33pp**) | | Nov 6 | claude_code (opus-5-5) | 212 / 1773 | 56% → 90% (**+34pp**) | | Nov 6 | antigravity_cli (gemini-4-argon) | 212 / 1722 | 60% → 96% (**+36pp**) | | Nov 4 | codex_cli (gpt-6.1-sol) | 209 / 1743 | 52% → 85% (**+33pp**) | | Nov 4 | claude_code (opus-5-5) | 209 / 1743 | 57% → 90% (**+33pp**) | | Nov 4 | antigravity_cli (gemini-4-argon) | 207 / 1722 | 60% → 96% (**+36pp**) | | Nov 2 | codex_cli (gpt-6.1-sol) | 205 / 1729 | 55% → 82% (**+27pp**) | ## Available Skill Packs You can customize which skill packs are installed using the `--choose` flag: ```shell npx modern-web-guidance@latest install --choose ``` * **`modern-web-guidance`** (~205 tokens): Comprehensive guidance on modern browser APIs, layouts, and performance. * **`chrome-extensions`** (~175 tokens): Guidance on Manifest V3, background workers, extension APIs, and Chrome Web Store publishing. ## Telemetry & Privacy Google collects anonymous usage information to improve the tool's reliability, relevance, and performance. Collected information includes installation counts, the calling agent name, guide retrieval IDs, and CLI tool search queries generated by the agent (e.g. "dark mode scrollbar color-scheme"). Raw user prompts are not collected. You can inspect what is collected in [modern-web.ts](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src/blob/main/src/cli/modern-web.ts). > [!TIP] > **To Opt-Out:** set the `DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1` env variable in your shell profile (e.g., `.bashrc` or `.zshrc`): > ```bash > export DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 > ``` Google handles this data in accordance with the [Google Privacy Policy](https://policies.google.com/privacy). ## Contributors Found a bug, outdated pattern, or missing web platform feature? [Open an issue](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src/issues) or see [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) in the [source repository (`GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src`)](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src). Huge thanks to everyone who has contributed! ## License Unless otherwise noted: * Software code in this project is licensed under the [Apache License 2.0](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src/blob/main/LICENSE). * Documentation and guide content under `guides/` are licensed under [Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC-BY 4.0)](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). repositories.readme:
Build your own AI office with Univer Office SDK.

Start with open-source Sheets and Docs, then connect your own application or agent.

🚀 Quick start · 💼 Workspace · 📚 Documentation · ⚖️ Feature comparison · 🌐 Website · 🎮 Showcase · 🔧 API Reference · 📝 Blog

English · Français · Deutsch · Español · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어

Table of contents - [💡 What is Univer?](#what-is-univer) - [Open-source capabilities](#open-source-capabilities) - [🚀 Build on the open-source foundation](#what-you-can-build) - [Quick start: an open-source spreadsheet editor](#quick-start) - [Connect your application to editable content](#connect-your-application-to-editable-content) - [🏗️ Explore the open-source architecture](#open-source-architecture) - [Give custom features clear boundaries](#give-custom-features-clear-boundaries) - [Compose cross-feature edits and undo/redo](#compose-cross-feature-edits-and-undoredo) - [Connect applications and agents through Facade APIs and events](#connect-applications-and-agents-through-facade-apis-and-events) - [🧩 Extend your application with Univer Office SDK](#open-source-and-commercial-extensions) - [Scope and licensing](#scope-and-licensing) - [🌐 Application patterns and ecosystem](#application-patterns-and-ecosystem) - [Univer Workspace: an Office SDK reference application](#univer-workspace-an-office-sdk-reference-application) - [CLI, agent integrations, and developer skills](#cli-agent-integrations-and-developer-skills) - [📚 Documentation and contributing](#documentation-and-contributing) - [Runtime compatibility](#runtime-compatibility) - [💬 Community](#community) - [🔒 Security](#security) - [❤️ Sponsors](#sponsors) - [📄 License](#license)
## 💡 What is Univer?

**Univer** is an Office SDK for building Office applications inside your own product. It provides Office editing, calculation, collaboration, and file processing for people and existing agents, using your data and permissions. The product family covers spreadsheets, documents, presentations, relational tables, canvases, and PDFs. Univer Office SDK has three parts: - **Web SDK** is the foundation: content models, editing, rendering, formula calculation, and Facade APIs (application-facing APIs). Compose its plugins into an embedded editor or your own Office application, and reuse the content models, commands, and calculation for Headless processing without an interactive editor. - **Server SDK** adds backend services for real-time collaboration, edit history, and Office file import and export. - **AI SDK** connects Office capabilities to existing agents and workflows, with content tools, execution, and review integrations. **This repository provides the Web SDK's core architecture and engine implementations under Apache-2.0**: content models and snapshot formats, plugin and dependency management, the command system, formula and rendering engines, Facade APIs, UI foundation, and Sheets and Docs editing capabilities. Commercial Web SDK plugins, Server SDK, and commercial AI SDK extensions are distributed and licensed separately. Agents can use the same open-source APIs; your application supplies the model and tool orchestration. The [quotation example](#connect-your-application-to-editable-content) demonstrates editing, calculation, and saving without an AI SDK dependency. ### Open-source capabilities
Area Selected capabilities
Sheets · Editing and layout Cell styles, merged cells, in-cell rich text, freeze panes, floating images, and undo/redo.
Sheets · Data and calculation Formulas, defined names, filtering, sorting, data validation, conditional formatting, hyperlinks, comments, and find and replace.
Docs Rich-text editing, paragraph formatting, lists, hyperlinks, comments, and drawing integration.
Features are composed through plugins and presets; the [quick start](#quick-start) uses only the **Sheets Core preset**. Images use the corresponding drawing plugins. See the [feature comparison](https://univer.ai/compare/) for detailed open-source and commercial coverage. The demos below showcase the wider **Univer Office SDK**, including commercial capabilities. They show more than the default open-source setup; see [open source and commercial extensions](#open-source-and-commercial-extensions) for scope.

## 🚀 Build on the open-source foundation

Your goal Use the open-source foundation Start here
Embed Sheets or Docs Add an editable Office surface to your application or agent product, and connect your data through Facade APIs. Quick start
Process content without an editor Reuse content plugins, models, commands, and calculation in Node.js for editing, snapshots, and automated tasks. Headless guide
Develop custom features or editors Reuse the engines, UI components, plugin boundaries, dependency injection, and command/undo systems. Follow existing features to extend Sheets and Docs or develop your own editors. Open-source architecture
**Coordinate edits and undo/redo across features.** Inserting a row inside a filter range changes both the base content and the filter range; undo needs to restore both. Each feature supplies its own changes and undo data, and the command composes their execution and history. The architecture walkthrough explains how to extend these editing workflows. ### Quick start: an open-source spreadsheet editor In a browser application using a bundler such as Vite: ```bash pnpm add @univerjs/presets @univerjs/preset-sheets-core ``` Create the container before initializing Univer: ```html
``` ```ts import { UniverSheetsCorePreset } from '@univerjs/preset-sheets-core' import UniverPresetSheetsCoreEnUS from '@univerjs/preset-sheets-core/locales/en-US' import { createUniver, LocaleType, mergeLocales } from '@univerjs/presets' import '@univerjs/preset-sheets-core/lib/index.css' const { univerAPI } = createUniver({ locale: LocaleType.EN_US, locales: { [LocaleType.EN_US]: mergeLocales(UniverPresetSheetsCoreEnUS), }, presets: [ UniverSheetsCorePreset({ container: 'app', }), ], }) univerAPI.createWorkbook({}) ``` Your page now contains a spreadsheet editor. Use the returned `univerAPI` to work with its content. This example uses open-source packages and needs no commercial Univer license or Server SDK. For component frameworks, retain the `univer` instance returned by `createUniver` and call `univer.dispose()` when the component unmounts. See the [lifecycle guide](https://docs.univer.ai/guides/sheets/getting-started/lifecycle). Presets compose plugins and register their Facade APIs. For manual control, see the [Plugin Mode example](#manual-plugin-composition) below. The [installation guide](https://docs.univer.ai/guides/sheets/getting-started/installation) covers both modes, peer dependencies, and framework integrations. Keep coordinated `@univerjs/*` packages on the same version. Commercial packages must use the matching release line; independently released packages such as icons follow their declared compatibility. See the [API Stability Policy](./docs/API_STABILITY.md). ### Connect your application to editable content Facade APIs are the application-facing interface to workbooks, worksheets, and ranges. Continue from the quick start to populate a quotation, update a quantity from application code, and read the recalculated total: ```ts // Wait for formula controllers before editing a newly created workbook. await new Promise((resolve) => { if (univerAPI.getCurrentLifecycleStage() >= univerAPI.Enum.LifecycleStages.Steady) { resolve() return } const listener = univerAPI.addEvent(univerAPI.Event.LifeCycleChanged, ({ stage }) => { if (stage === univerAPI.Enum.LifecycleStages.Steady) { listener.dispose() resolve() } }) }) const workbook = univerAPI.getActiveWorkbook()! const sheet = workbook.getActiveSheet() sheet.getRange('A1:D4').setValues([ ['Item', 'Quantity', 'Unit price', 'Amount'], ['Seats', 2, 25, '=B2*C2'], ['Support', 1, 100, '=B3*C3'], ['Total', '', '', '=SUM(D2:D3)'], ]) // An application control or agent can make the same edit. sheet.getRange('B2').setValue(4) univerAPI.getFormula().onCalculationResultApplied().then(() => { console.log(sheet.getRange('D4').getValue()) // 200 localStorage.setItem('quotation', JSON.stringify(workbook.save())) }).catch(console.error) ``` The editor and your application operate on the same workbook; formula changes are recalculated automatically. `workbook.save()` returns a JSON snapshot containing the workbook and its registered plugin data. Your application owns persistence; this example uses browser storage. On a later page load, after initialization, restore the snapshot **instead of creating a blank workbook**: ```ts const saved = localStorage.getItem('quotation') if (saved) { univerAPI.createWorkbook(JSON.parse(saved)) } ``` This workflow uses only open-source packages. Snapshot persistence is separate from XLSX import and export, which uses the separately distributed file-conversion capabilities. Use public Facade APIs for application integration; the source links below explain internal implementation and extension points. See the [API Stability Policy](./docs/API_STABILITY.md) before depending on an extension point.
Advanced: compose plugins manually (Plugin Mode) Use Plugin Mode when you need precise control over plugin selection, dependencies, or loading. The preset above handles this composition for you. This alternative initialization uses the same `app` container and the Sheets Core preset's browser plugin stack without a Worker. Use it **instead of** the preset initialization, then run the same quotation example with the returned `univerAPI`. ```bash pnpm add @univerjs/core @univerjs/design @univerjs/docs @univerjs/docs-ui \ @univerjs/engine-formula @univerjs/engine-render @univerjs/network \ @univerjs/sheets @univerjs/sheets-ui @univerjs/sheets-formula \ @univerjs/sheets-formula-ui @univerjs/sheets-numfmt \ spreadsheet rich-text editing. When adding a feature, include its corresponding Facade extensions, locale bundles, and UI styles. Dispose `univer` when its container is unmounted.

## 🏗️ Explore the open-source architecture

### Give custom features clear boundaries Univer organizes content logic and UI interaction in separate plugins. Feature plugins manage rules and content changes; UI plugins provide the interface and user interactions. For example, `sheets-filter` manages filter ranges and rules, while `sheets-filter-ui` provides panels, menus, and shortcuts. ```mermaid %%{init: {'htmlLabels': false, 'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': {'fontFamily': 'Arial, PingFang SC, Microsoft YaHei, sans-serif', 'fontSize': '17px', 'lineColor': '#64748b'}, 'flowchart': {'htmlLabels': false, 'curve': 'linear', 'nodeSpacing': 28, 'rankSpacing': 45, 'padding': 16, 'wrappingWidth': 270}}}%% %% A layered overview, not a complete dependency graph. %% Group arrows indicate reuse of the layer below; internal arrows show selected dependencies. flowchart TD subgraph FEATURES["Feature Plugins"] direction LR FUI["Filter
UI Plugin"] VUI["Data Validation
UI Plugin"] FILTER["Filter Plugin"] VALIDATION["Data Validation Plugin"] FUI --> FILTER VUI --> VALIDATION end subgraph PRODUCTS["Product Plugins"] direction LR SUI["Sheets UI Plugin"] SHEETS["Sheets Plugin"] SUI --> SHEETS end subgraph FOUNDATION["Core Framework & Plugins"] direction LR UI["UI Plugin"] FORMULA["Formula Engine Plugin"] RENDER["Render Engine Plugin"] CORE["Core"] UI --> RENDER RENDER --> CORE FORMULA --> CORE end FEATURES --> PRODUCTS PRODUCTS --> FOUNDATION classDef logic fill:#eff6ff,color:#17365f,stroke:#93b4df,stroke-width:1.5px classDef ui fill:#f0fdf4,color:#17543a,stroke:#91c8a7,stroke-width:1.5px classDef shared fill:#f6f7f9,color:#334155,stroke:#bac3ce,stroke-width:1.5px classDef feature fill:#172d50,color:#ffffff,stroke:#172d50 class FUI,VUI ui class FILTER,VALIDATION logic class SUI,SHEETS logic class UI,FORMULA,RENDER,CORE shared style FEATURES fill:#f7fcf9,stroke:#b5d8c1,color:#17543a style PRODUCTS fill:#f5f9ff,stroke:#b6cbea,color:#17365f style FOUNDATION fill:#fafbfc,stroke:#cbd2dc,color:#334155 ``` **Figure 1: three plugin layers.** Feature plugins build on product plugins, which reuse the core framework and plugins. Group arrows show dependencies on the layer below; Core provides content models, commands, dependency injection, and lifecycle management. Some plugins and dependencies are omitted. New features keep their rules in their own plugins and cooperate through public services, commands, and defined extension points. UI plugins build on shared UI services and components. Dependencies are explicit at two levels: - **Between plugins:** `DependentOn` declares runtime plugin dependencies. The plugin service orders them, and lifecycle stages separate dependency registration, content initialization, and UI initialization. - **Inside plugins:** dependency injection connects controllers and services through declared dependencies. Supported overrides let an application replace an implementation, adapt a platform service, or supply a test double. Instance-scoped injectors keep application state separate between Univer instances. Disposable registration also gives commands, listeners, components, and icons a cleanup path when their owner is disposed. The [filter plugin](./packages/sheets-filter/src/plugin.ts) and its [UI plugin](./packages/sheets-filter-ui/src/plugin.ts) show these boundaries in working code.
Inside a feature: Model, Controller, Service, and the UI foundation For filtering, `sheets-filter` owns content logic and `sheets-filter-ui` owns UI interaction. Each module has a focused responsibility. ```mermaid %%{init: {'htmlLabels': false, 'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': {'fontFamily': 'Arial, PingFang SC, Microsoft YaHei, sans-serif', 'fontSize': '17px', 'lineColor': '#64748b'}, 'flowchart': {'htmlLabels': false, 'curve': 'linear', 'nodeSpacing': 28, 'rankSpacing': 45, 'padding': 16, 'wrappingWidth': 270}}}%% %% Every arrow means contains. This is code organization, not execution order. flowchart LR FEATURE["Filter Feature"] LOGIC["Filter Plugin"] UI["Filter UI Plugin"] MODEL["Model"] SERVICE["Service"] CONTROLLER["Controller"] COMMAND["Command / Mutation"] FACADE["Facade API"] VIEW["View"] UICTRL["UI Controller"] UISERVICE["UI Service"] FEATURE --> LOGIC FEATURE --> UI LOGIC --> MODEL LOGIC --> SERVICE LOGIC --> CONTROLLER LOGIC --> COMMAND LOGIC --> FACADE UI --> VIEW UI --> UICTRL UI --> UISERVICE classDef logic fill:#eff6ff,color:#17365f,stroke:#93b4df,stroke-width:1.5px classDef ui fill:#f0fdf4,color:#17543a,stroke:#91c8a7,stroke-width:1.5px classDef shared fill:#f6f7f9,color:#334155,stroke:#bac3ce,stroke-width:1.5px classDef feature fill:#172d50,color:#ffffff,stroke:#172d50 class FEATURE feature class LOGIC,MODEL,SERVICE,CONTROLLER,COMMAND,FACADE logic class UI,VIEW,UICTRL,UISERVICE ui ``` **Figure 2: code organization. Arrows mean “contains.”** Both plugins can contain Controllers and Services: logic Controllers coordinate content changes and related features; UI Controllers connect menus, shortcuts, and interactions, with UI Services managing panel state. These responsibilities give new features a consistent structure to implement and test. The UI foundation follows the same division. **`@univerjs/design`** supplies shared components and styles, **`@univerjs/ui`** provides workbench services such as menus, shortcuts, panels, and component registration, and **`@univerjs/icons`** supplies icons. A feature registers its components and icons, contributes menus, and attaches its rendering through these extension points. Teams can add a panel or toolbar feature while reusing the application's UI infrastructure. See the [UI overview](https://docs.univer.ai/guides/sheets/ui/overview) and the filter plugin's [component and icon registration](./packages/sheets-filter-ui/src/controllers/components.controller.ts).
### Compose cross-feature edits and undo/redo For example, when rows are inserted inside a filter range, the filter plugin supplies the corresponding range change and its undo data. The row command composes the base edit and participating feature changes, executes them, and records their undo/redo information together. The row insertion feature can use the shared extension mechanism while the filter plugin owns its range-update rules. The command system distinguishes three kinds of action: - **Command** orchestrates a business action and the changes it requires. - **Mutation** changes content saved in a snapshot, with serializable parameters. - **Operation** changes transient state, such as an open panel or the scroll position. **A shared structure for undo/redo.** For an undoable edit, the feature implementation supplies the forward mutations and corresponding inverse mutations, and the Command records them through `IUndoRedoService`. When one action affects several features, the Command can combine their changes and undo data in a single undo/redo record, so the user can undo and redo the complete action. See [extending commands](https://docs.univer.ai/blog/custom-command). Features still need to cooperate. **Interceptors and reference-range handlers give that cooperation a defined place.** At supported extension points, plugins contribute checks or related mutations; interceptor priorities control ordering where the API defines it.
Example: commands, callbacks, feature coordination, and undo/redo ```mermaid %%{init: {'htmlLabels': false, 'theme': 'base', 'themeVariables': {'fontFamily': 'Arial, PingFang SC, Microsoft YaHei, sans-serif', 'fontSize': '17px', 'lineColor': '#64748b'}, 'flowchart': {'htmlLabels': false, 'curve': 'linear', 'nodeSpacing': 28, 'rankSpacing': 45, 'padding': 16, 'wrappingWidth': 270}}}%% %% Simplified insert-row example. A command composes mutations and records undo after success. %% Events may also fire for nested command executions; not every callback is drawn. flowchart TD BEFORE["Before execution
Inspect or cancel"] CMD["Insert-row Command"] BASE["Row mutations"] EXT["Feature extension points
Filter range changes"] MODEL["Execute combined mutations"] UNDO["Record undo and redo"] AFTER["After execution
Notify listeners"] BEFORE --> CMD CMD --> BASE CMD --> EXT BASE --> MODEL EXT --> MODEL MODEL --> UNDO UNDO --> AFTER classDef entry fill:#f6f7f9,color:#334155,stroke:#bac3ce,stroke-width:1.5px classDef core fill:#eff6ff,color:#17365f,stroke:#93b4df,stroke-width:1.5px classDef extension fill:#f0fdf4,color:#17543a,stroke:#91c8a7,stroke-width:1.5px class BEFORE,AFTER entry class CMD,BASE,MODEL,UNDO core class EXT extension ``` This diagram simplifies an insert-row workflow. Nested command executions have their own callbacks; it does not show every event or the separate Operation path. See the [row command](./packages/sheets/src/commands/commands/insert-row-col.command.ts), [filter controller](./packages/sheets-filter/src/controllers/sheets-filter.controller.ts), and [interceptor service](./packages/sheets/src/services/sheet-interceptor/sheet-interceptor.service.ts).
These boundaries support a practical testing strategy: test models and services independently, replace external dependencies through DI, and add regression cases for combined actions and undo/redo. The [filter controller tests](./packages/sheets-filter/src/controllers/__tests__/sheets-filter.controller.spec.ts) exercise row and column changes and their effect on filtering. ### Connect applications and agents through Facade APIs and events The repository includes the content models, formula engine, and Canvas rendering and layout engine behind the editors. They are shared building blocks: spreadsheet rich text, for example, reuses document layout and rendering. Custom features can build on these engines instead of implementing a separate content stack. Read about the [formula engine architecture](https://docs.univer.ai/blog/formula) and [rendering engine architecture](https://docs.univer.ai/blog/rendering). Browser editors, Node.js Headless tasks, and appropriately composed Workers can reuse the corresponding content plugins, models, commands, and calculation. See [Headless Univer](https://docs.univer.ai/guides/sheets/getting-started/node) and the [isomorphic architecture](./docs/ISOMORPHIC.md). `ICommandService` exposes execution callbacks so plugins can observe commands before and after execution. Facade APIs wrap the underlying capabilities in application objects such as `FWorkbook`, `FWorksheet`, and `FRange`. Each plugin contributes its own Facade extensions, **typed events through `univerAPI.Event`**, and **enums through `univerAPI.Enum`**. Application code can discover event names and constants from one entry point instead of importing private services or repeating strings. For example, `BeforeCommandExecute` can inspect and cancel an execution; `CommandExecuted` reports executions to listeners. Listeners return disposables, and cancellation applies where the event supports it. Facade extensions stay with their feature packages, so a content API does not have to pull in unrelated UI APIs. See the [Facade design](https://docs.univer.ai/blog/facade), [command callbacks and event bridge](./packages/core/src/facade/f-univer.ts), and [Enum entry point](./packages/core/src/facade/f-enum.ts). The repository provides working feature implementations and patterns for extending them. Read the [filter implementation walkthrough](https://docs.univer.ai/blog/anatomy) for a complete example, or the [API Stability Policy](./docs/API_STABILITY.md) before depending on an extension point.

## 🧩 Extend your application with Univer Office SDK

When you want more ready-to-integrate capabilities, compose the corresponding **Univer Office SDK** modules: additional content types, advanced editing plugins, collaboration, file conversion, and agent tooling. They extend the same content models, plugin architecture, command system, and Facade design introduced above, so you can build on your existing integration.
Part How it extends the foundation
Open-source Web SDK core · this repository Open-source models, engines, plugins, UI foundation, and Sheets and Docs capabilities, with corresponding Headless content operations. Use them in commercial applications under Apache-2.0.
Commercial Web SDK plugins Follow the core's Plugin, dependency injection, Command/Mutation, and Facade extension patterns. Add charts, shapes, pivot tables, SmartArt, and other features for the corresponding content types.
Server SDK Extends the same content models and mutation conventions with real-time collaboration, revision history, and Office file conversion. Integrates with your application's identity, permissions, and storage.
AI SDK extensions Reuse Web SDK Headless and Facade capabilities to provide composable Node.js APIs and CLI building blocks for agents to inspect, edit, and check content, with collaboration and Worktree review integrations.
### Scope and licensing - **This repository:** Apache-2.0 packages that can be used in commercial applications under that license, including the open-source Headless content capabilities. - **Commercial extensions:** Commercial Web SDK plugins, Server SDK, and AI SDK capabilities beyond the open-source foundation are distributed and licensed separately. **Freemium** evaluation includes watermarks and feature limits. - **Reference applications:** Open-source applications such as Univer Workspace have their own source licenses. Their SDK dependencies retain their respective licenses. See the [feature comparison](https://univer.ai/compare/), including its **Open source only** filter, for detailed coverage and [plans and licensing](https://univer.ai/pricing/) for commercial options.
How shared content models connect editing, collaboration, and files These capabilities operate on serializable **Unit snapshots**, including Sheets' `IWorkbookData`, Docs' `IDocumentData`, Slides' `ISlideData`, and canvases' `IBoardData` (called **Boards** in the API). These types come from core and the respective product packages; current Slides and Boards capabilities are separately distributed commercial products. The shared Unit conventions let browser editors, backend services, and agents work with the same content. Commands orchestrate edits; **Mutations describe content changes**. Collaboration packages those mutations into **changesets**, applies **operational transformation (OT)** to concurrent changes, and manages confirmed revisions and snapshots. History can reconstruct a revision from a snapshot and subsequent changesets. Read the [collaboration design](https://docs.univer.ai/blog/ot) and [Collaboration SDK overview](https://docs.univer.ai/server/collaboration/overview). **Exchange** maps Office file structures to and from Univer content snapshots. For OOXML formats such as **XLSX, DOCX, and PPTX**, it parses the file into the corresponding Sheet, Doc, or Slide data and generates the file representation on export. The converted content can enter the same editing, calculation, collaboration, and agent workflows. See [Office file import and export](https://docs.univer.ai/server/import-export/node).
How AI SDK gives agents the same content capabilities AI SDK builds on the Web SDK's **Headless content models, commands, calculation, and Facade APIs**. It exposes structured TypeScript APIs and optional Commander presets that applications can compose into their own Office CLI or agent tools. - **Understand, discover, and edit.** Inspection returns structured content. API Reference helps the agent find Facade symbols and signatures shipped with its SDK. Facade execution distinguishes read and write modes, captures mutations, and works with explicit synchronization and commit results. See [content operations](https://docs.univer.ai/ai/content-operations). - **Check the rendered result.** A browser Render Runtime reuses Web SDK rendering for screenshots. Slide layout lint adds structured findings for issues such as off-page or overlapping text, giving the agent evidence for another editing pass. See [visual inspection](https://docs.univer.ai/ai/visual-inspection). - **Edit drafts for human review.** With the corresponding collaboration and Web capabilities, agents can edit and verify an isolated Worktree draft over several rounds, then hand it to a person to review, merge, or reopen. The workflow uses the same snapshots, mutations, and revision conventions. See [Worktree](https://docs.univer.ai/ai/worktree). For repeated calls, optional [Worker pools and a daemon](https://docs.univer.ai/ai/runtime-architecture) reuse loaded content instances and reduce repeated initialization. Your application owns the root CLI, targets, authorization, and output. Explore the [AI SDK package catalog](https://docs.univer.ai/ai/packages) to select the required capabilities.

## 🌐 Application patterns and ecosystem

Follow its integration patterns when building your own Office application or agent workspace.

Each repository documents its setup and SDK dependencies. Explore the [ecosystem](https://univer.ai/ecosystem/) for agent entry points, or the [documentation](https://docs.univer.ai/) to build your own integration.

Univer is compiled with a Chrome 88 target and aims to work with the versions listed above.

### Runtime compatibility - **Polyfills**: Univer relies on `Intl.Segmenter`. Add a polyfill such as `@formatjs/intl-segmenter` if your target browser or runtime does not provide it. - **Build tools**: We recommend Vite, esbuild, or Webpack 5. If your build tool does not support the `exports` field in `package.json` (common in Webpack 4), you may need extra path mapping. - **React**: Univer's view layer is built on React 18, supports React 18 and 19, and provides minimal compatibility support for React 16.9+ and 17. - **Node.js runtime**: Headless Univer supports Node.js `>=18.17.0`. Developing this monorepo requires Node.js `>=22.18`.

# Plannotator **⭐️ NEW:** [Plannotator Inbox](https://plannotator.ai/inbox/) is the missing review layer between you and multi-agent work. It surfaces decisions, prototypes, variations, plans, and everything you need to stay in the loop. Works with all coding agents and personal assistants. Plannotator is a local, browser-based review surface for AI coding agents: Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Kiro, Droid, Amp, DeepSeek Harness, and Pi. Plannotator Inbox also works with personal assistants (Grok Bot, Muse, Hermes, OpenClaw). **It plugs directly into your agent** through plugins, hooks and commands. When the agent proposes a decision, plan, html, or finishes working, the app opens in your browser and you mark it up, comment, and send feedback directly to the agent for it to act on it.
### Review documents, plans, and agent messages Annotate plans, specs, messages, html, then send the feedback to your agent.
### Code Review Review local changes or remote PRs. Comment on diffs, suggest code. Your comments go back to the agent. Works with Git, GitButler, Jujutsu (`jj`), Perforce (`p4`), GitHub, and GitLab.
## Plannotator Inbox

Watch the demo · More on the Inbox · Docs

The Plannotator Inbox is one local window where your agents leave you messages, questions, files, and guided reviews while they keep working. Answer a question with a click, annotate a file, and press Send when you can. Nothing holds an agent session open while you do, and your reply goes back to the session that asked. ``` plannotator inbox ``` Claude Code, Pi, and OpenCode connect through Plannotator's plugins, and your replies arrive as their next turn. Any other agent reaches it over MCP with `plannotator inbox mcp`, and `plannotator inbox --help` is the guide an agent reads. ## Herdr Annotate: Plannotator in the Terminal

  

[Herdr Annotate](https://github.com/plannotator/herdr-annotate) brings Plannotator-style review to the terminal: annotate terminal text, review whole Markdown documents and your coding agent's replies inside [Herdr](https://herdr.dev), and send the feedback straight back to the agent as its next message. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Copilot CLI, and Droid replies. Annotations are saved in the Plannotator data directory, so terminal reviews and app reviews compound. ``` herdr plugin install plannotator/herdr-annotate ``` Prefer it standalone? [Plannotator TUI](https://github.com/plannotator/plannotator-tui) powers the document review and runs without Herdr: `brew install plannotator/tap/plannotator-tui`. ## Annotate HTML Artifacts

--- ## Commands On Codex, swap the slash commands for `!plannotator …` (e.g. `!plannotator review`) or the `$plannotator-*` skills. ### Annotate ``` /plannotator-annotate README.md # Local markdown file /plannotator-annotate src/ # Browse and annotate files in a folder /plannotator-annotate https://docs.rs/… # Fetch and annotate any URL /plannotator-annotate report.html --render-html # Render HTML as-is instead of converting /plannotator-last # Annotate the agent's last message ``` Need a realistic document to try? Copy the [product requirements document template and filled example](https://docs.plannotator.ai/templates/product-requirements-document) as Markdown. ### Code review ``` /plannotator-review # Review uncommitted changes /plannotator-review # Review a GitHub pull request /plannotator-review # Review a GitLab merge request plannotator review --gitbutler # Review an active GitButler workspace plannotator review --patch-file reading.diff # Review a static caller-supplied unified diff ``` GitButler users can review the whole workspace, one stack, or one branch layer. See the [GitButler workflow guide](https://docs.plannotator.ai/open-source/workflows/gitbutler). ### Plan mode No command needed. Plan mode is wired in through each harness's hooks. Any time your agent creates a plan, the markdown review surface opens for you. ### CLI ``` plannotator sessions # List active Plannotator sessions plannotator sessions --open 1 # Reopen a session in the browser plannotator archive # Browse saved plan decisions read-only ``` --- ## AI built in Ask AI about anything you're reviewing, or launch AI reviews that post comments to the diff. --- ## Sharing Send a plan as a link. A teammate annotates it, and you import their feedback for your agent. Small shares live in the link itself. Large ones are encrypted before upload and expire after 7 days. Anyone with the full link can read it. Turn sharing off with `PLANNOTATOR_SHARE=disabled`. [How sharing works](https://docs.plannotator.ai/open-source/workflows/sharing)

--- ## Install One installer covers almost every agent. It installs the `plannotator` binary, auto-detects your installed agents, and configures hooks, skills, and slash commands for each: ```bash # macOS / Linux / WSL curl -fsSL https://plannotator.ai/install.sh | bash ``` ```powershell # Windows PowerShell irm https://plannotator.ai/install.ps1 | iex ``` The installer downloads the binary from GitHub Releases. A full install can also contact GitHub for release resolution and agent files, Ataraxy-Labs/sem for the optional `sem` sidecar, and npm for Pi, selected extra skills, or the managed agent-terminal runtime. Pinning `--version` skips only GitHub API release resolution, not the release download. See the [privacy policy](https://plannotator.ai/privacy) for the complete network boundaries. Want just the binary and nothing else? Pass `--minimal` (or export `PLANNOTATOR_MINIMAL=1`) to install only the `plannotator` binary to `~/.local/bin`, skipping every skill, hook, slash command, and per-agent config: ```bash curl -fsSL https://plannotator.ai/install.sh | bash -s -- --minimal ``` Then finish the step for your agent: | Agent | After the installer | Details | |---|---|---| | **Amp** | Copy [`plannotator.ts`](apps/amp-plugin/plannotator.ts) into `~/.config/amp/plugins/`, then `plugins: reload`. Workflows live in the command palette. | [README](apps/amp-plugin/README.md) | | **Claude Code** | `/plugin marketplace add backnotprop/plannotator`, then `/plugin install plannotator@plannotator`. Restart Claude Code. | [README](apps/hook/README.md) | | **Codex** | Nothing. Plan review is enabled automatically via Codex's experimental `Stop` hook (macOS/Linux/WSL; on native Windows, Codex hooks are experimental and the installer prints manual setup steps). `$plannotator-review`, `$plannotator-annotate`, and `$plannotator-last` skills included. | [README](apps/codex/README.md) | | **Copilot CLI** | `/plugin marketplace add backnotprop/plannotator`, then `/plugin install plannotator-copilot@plannotator`. Restart. Plan review activates in plan mode (`Shift+Tab`). | [README](apps/copilot/README.md) | | **DeepSeek Harness** | Add `@plannotator/dsh` on DSH's Plugins page, or run `dsh plugin --profile add @plannotator/dsh`. Plan review opens on `exit_plan_mode`. The plugin adds `/plannotator-review`, `/plannotator-annotate` and `/plannotator-last`, which open without blocking the session. | [README](apps/dsh-plugin/README.md) | | **Droid** | `droid plugin marketplace add https://github.com/backnotprop/plannotator`, then `droid plugin install plannotator@plannotator`. Commands only, no plan interception yet. | [README](apps/droid-plugin/README.md) | | **Gemini CLI** | Nothing. The hook, policy, and slash commands are configured automatically. Requires Gemini CLI 0.36.0+. | [README](apps/gemini/README.md) | | **Kiro CLI** | Nothing. Skills and an example agent are installed automatically. Try `kiro-cli chat --agent plannotator`. | [README](apps/kiro-cli/README.md) | | **OpenCode** | Add `"plugin": ["@plannotator/opencode@latest"]` to `opencode.json`. Restart OpenCode. | [README](apps/opencode-plugin/README.md) | | **Pi** | Skip the installer. Just `pi install npm:@plannotator/pi-extension`. Start Pi with `--plan`, or toggle with `/plannotator-plan-mode`. | [README](apps/pi-extension/README.md) | | **T3 Code** | For Claude threads in T3: run `plannotator t3 --help` and follow its two steps (sign in to T3 once, add the `--t3` MCP entry). Your Inbox replies then arrive in the thread as new turns. | [README](packages/t3-code/README.md) | **Updating:** run the installer again for the binary and slash commands. It also updates an installed Claude Code plugin when the `claude` command is on your PATH (opt out with `--skip-claude-plugin`); otherwise run `claude plugin marketplace update plannotator`, then `claude plugin update plannotator@plannotator`, then restart Claude Code (refreshing the marketplace alone does not update the plugin). Pi: `pi update --extensions` (a plain `pi update` updates only Pi). On Claude Code 2.1.287 or newer, plan review, code review and annotate don't make Claude wait: Claude ends its turn and your decision arrives later as a message. Set `PLANNOTATOR_CLAUDE_MOD=0` to go back to the classic flow. Full walkthroughs live in the [installation docs](https://docs.plannotator.ai/open-source/start/installation). ### Uninstall The safe default removes recognized Plannotator-installed components and keeps your local plans, history, drafts, guides, and settings: ```bash plannotator uninstall ``` Use `--purge` for a full removal of known local Plannotator data as well: ```bash plannotator uninstall --purge ``` Purge requires typing `purge` at the prompt and explains that the data is local-only: it is not stored on a Plannotator server and cannot be recovered. For automation, pass `--yes` (or `-y`); non-interactive removal refuses to run without it. Use `--dry-run` to preview recognized work without making changes. Host integrations are always part of uninstall. If a broken or unavailable host prevents safe cleanup, the command names the blocking plugin manager or configuration, gives exact manual cleanup instructions, and stops before deleting the binary. Complete that cleanup and rerun uninstall. It also keeps the binary when an agent's config file can't be read (another tool's too), or when a hook it did not install still runs Plannotator. The error names the file, the tool, and what to do. A `plannotator-inbox` entry you added yourself, or a Claude Code or Droid plugin installed for one project, is named with how to remove it and does not keep the binary. These mechanics keep the ordinary confirmation default-negative, make the irreversible outcome require a stronger explicit word, and still give package managers and scripts a conventional non-interactive flag. The command covers the conventional macOS, Linux, WSL, and Windows binary locations; the managed `sem` sidecar and agent-terminal runtime; installer skills, commands, hooks, policies, caches, and recognizable Amp/Kiro files; and detected Claude Code, Copilot CLI, Droid, Pi, and VS Code installations through their host CLIs. Shared JSONC settings are edited surgically, while strict JSON updates preserve the file's indentation, line endings, and trailing-newline style. Custom or unrecognized files, separately installed optional skills, project-local integrations, external plan-save locations, and invalid configs are preserved (malformed host config is a fail-safe error). If cleanup reports an error, the CLI remains available for a safe retry, and its Windows PATH entry is retained or restored when possible. If PATH restoration itself fails, the output gives the full CLI path for retry and asks for manual PATH repair. For safety, purge refuses filesystem roots, the home directory, the shared temporary directory, symlinked data directories, and non-directory data paths. Existing paths are compared by filesystem identity, so case aliases, symlinks, hardlinks, and bind mounts cannot bypass the root/home/ancestor checks. That identity and every containment guard are revalidated after awaited host commands, immediately before the synchronous data-removal block; a replaced data directory is refused without touching either the old or replacement data. If your dedicated data directory is symlinked, point `PLANNOTATOR_DATA_DIR` at its resolved target and retry. If you installed only the standalone Pi extension and do not have the `plannotator` CLI, use `pi remove npm:@plannotator/pi-extension`.
Claude Code: manual hook setup (without the plugin system) Add to `~/.claude/settings.json`: ```json { "hooks": { "PermissionRequest": [ { "matcher": "ExitPlanMode", "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "plannotator", "timeout": 345600 } ] } ] } } ```
Pin a specific version ```bash curl -fsSL https://plannotator.ai/install.sh | bash -s -- --version vX.Y.Z ``` ```powershell & ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://plannotator.ai/install.ps1))) -Version vX.Y.Z ```
### Try it The fastest way to see what Plannotator does is to invoke it yourself, right now, from your agent: ``` /plannotator-last # annotate the agent's last reply /plannotator-review # review your current diff, PR-style /plannotator-annotate report.html # annotate any file, folder, or URL ``` (Slash commands in most agents; `$plannotator-*` skills in Codex, command palette in Amp.) Plan review needs no command at all. The next time your agent proposes a plan, it opens in your browser automatically. --- ## How it works ### Plan review ``` Agent calls ExitPlanMode -> PermissionRequest hook fires -> Local server reads plan from hook input -> Browser opens with review UI -> You annotate and approve/deny -> Approve: agent proceeds -> Deny: structured feedback sent to agent -> Agent revises, plan diff shows what changed ``` ### Code review ``` You run /plannotator-review -> git diff captures changes (or PR fetched by URL) -> Browser opens with diff viewer -> Annotate lines, stage/unstage files -> Send feedback: returned to agent session -> Approve: "LGTM" sent ``` --- ## Integrations **VS Code**: Open plans in editor tabs, view diffs inline, add annotations from the editor gutter. Install from the [VS Code Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=backnotprop.plannotator-webview). **Obsidian**: Auto-save approved plans to a vault with YAML frontmatter, tags from the plan title, and backlinks for graph connectivity. Configure in Plannotator's Settings panel. **Bear**: Save plans as Bear notes with nested tags and project metadata. **Notion**: Save plans as Markdown child pages under a shared Notion page. Set `NOTION_TOKEN` in the environment that starts Plannotator, then configure the parent page in Settings. **GitHub / GitLab**: Pass any PR or MR URL to `/plannotator-review` and review it with the full diff viewer, annotations, and file tree. --- ## Remote / SSH / devcontainer Plannotator auto-detects SSH sessions and switches to fixed port `19432`. For a different port, or in a devcontainer or Docker: ```bash export PLANNOTATOR_REMOTE=1 export PLANNOTATOR_PORT=9999 # forward this port ``` VS Code devcontainers forward the port automatically (check the Ports tab). For raw SSH, add this to `~/.ssh/config`, using your `PLANNOTATOR_PORT` value if you set one: ``` Host your-server LocalForward 19432 localhost:19432 ``` In remote mode the server listens on every interface (`0.0.0.0`) with no login, so anyone who can reach the port can use it, even when you use an SSH tunnel. Keep the port closed to networks you don't trust. --- ## Security Every released binary ships with a SHA256 sidecar. [SLSA provenance](https://slsa.dev/) attestations are available from v0.17.2. The current release workflow also attaches a CycloneDX JSON SBOM, evaluates it with a fresh Grype database before anything is attested or published, and creates a GitHub/Sigstore SBOM attestation for the shipped binaries and npm tarballs. The SBOM is intentionally labeled as a release-wide Syft inventory of the monorepo's locked build inputs and dependencies. It is not an exact per-binary runtime inventory: Bun standalone executables do not expose their bundled JavaScript package metadata to Syft. The canonical [installation and verification docs](https://docs.plannotator.ai/open-source/start/installation#pin-or-verify-a-release) cover the existing installer path; the exact new SBOM commands are included below and must be copied to that Mintlify page before the first SBOM-enabled release. The release gate rejects scanner-side ignored matches and treats unknown applicability conservatively as runtime when evaluating CISA KEV and fixable Critical findings. Its explicit Grype configuration, complete JSON results, database status, and repository policy decision remain available as workflow evidence. To verify a released Linux x64 binary, its existing provenance, and the new SBOM evidence directly: ```bash tag=vX.Y.Z version="${tag#v}" mkdir -p /tmp/plannotator-release-verify gh release download "$tag" --repo backnotprop/plannotator \ --pattern 'plannotator-linux-x64*' \ --pattern "plannotator-${version}-release-sbom.cdx.json*" \ --dir /tmp/plannotator-release-verify (cd /tmp/plannotator-release-verify && sha256sum --check plannotator-linux-x64.sha256) (cd /tmp/plannotator-release-verify && sha256sum --check "plannotator-${version}-release-sbom.cdx.json.sha256") gh attestation verify /tmp/plannotator-release-verify/plannotator-linux-x64 \ --repo backnotprop/plannotator --source-ref "refs/tags/$tag" \ --signer-workflow backnotprop/plannotator/.github/workflows/release.yml \ --predicate-type https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1 gh attestation verify /tmp/plannotator-release-verify/plannotator-linux-x64 \ --repo backnotprop/plannotator --source-ref "refs/tags/$tag" \ --signer-workflow backnotprop/plannotator/.github/workflows/release.yml \ --predicate-type https://cyclonedx.org/bom ``` These are separate claims over the same artifact digest: provenance identifies its builder/source/workflow, while the CycloneDX predicate describes the release-wide inventory. The release runbook also canonicalizes the downloaded SBOM and attested predicate with `jq -S` and compares them. To verify on install: ```bash curl -fsSL https://plannotator.ai/install.sh | bash -s -- --verify-attestation ``` Requires the `gh` CLI, but no login: the installer fetches the attestation bundle from GitHub's public attestations API and verifies it with `gh attestation verify --bundle` (the extraction needs node, python3, or jq on PATH; gh's authenticated fetch is the fallback). Can also be set persistently in `~/.plannotator/config.json`: ```json { "verifyAttestation": true } ``` Installer verification remains opt-in and verifies SLSA build provenance; normal installation does not require `gh`. See the [canonical installation docs](https://docs.plannotator.ai/open-source/start/installation#pin-or-verify-a-release) for details. --- ## Configuration Settings are saved in cookies (not localStorage) because each hook invocation runs on a random port. You can also set options through environment variables or `~/.plannotator/config.json`. ### Optional Vim controls Plan and annotate views offer a default-off **Vim controls** profile under **Settings → Vim**. Once enabled, focus the document and use `j` / `k` to move one rendered block at a time. After `l` refines into a semantic level, `j` / `k` move among sibling rows, cells, or inline targets; `h` moves back to the containing target. Refining past the deepest target enters text. `v` starts characterwise Visual selection and `V` selects whole blocks. `Space` opens the normal annotation toolbar; `c`, `d`, `m`, and `t` select comment, redline, markup, and label actions. The same semantic target graph drives pointer Pinpoint and keyboard navigation. Press `?` in the document for the contextual key reference. Inputs, dialogs, editors, `Tab`, and all pointer interactions retain their native behavior. The document takes focus automatically when the page is otherwise neutral; press `Escape` from app chrome to return to it without clicking. An additional default-off **Vim HUD** toggle appears beneath Vim controls. It uses the product-demo styling for the live target reticle and navigation context. Its bottom-right **Key panel** is independently hideable while the reticle remains active; `?` still opens the complete key map on demand. The panel shows recent handled keys, the current block/line/word/Visual phase, and the command meaning without capturing text typed into comments or other controls. See [Vim controls](docs/vim-controls.md) for the interaction contract and implementation architecture. | Variable | Description | |---|---| | `PLANNOTATOR_REMOTE` | `1`/`true` for remote mode, `0`/`false` for local, unset for SSH auto-detection | | `PLANNOTATOR_PORT` | Fixed port (default: random locally, `19432` remote) | | `PLANNOTATOR_BROWSER` | Custom browser to open plans in. `none` (also `false`, `0`, `off`, `no`, `true`, `1`, `:`) opens no browser at all; the session URL is always printed. | | `PLANNOTATOR_AI` | `disabled` to disable Ask AI, Review Agents, and Guided Review; the annotate agent terminal is separate | | `PLANNOTATOR_SHARE` | `disabled` to turn off URL sharing | | `PLANNOTATOR_SHARE_URL` | Custom base URL for share links (self-hosted portal) | | `PLANNOTATOR_PASTE_URL` | Base URL of the paste service API | | `PLANNOTATOR_ORIGIN` | Override agent detection: `claude-code`, `amp`, `droid`, `opencode`, `codex`, `copilot-cli`, `gemini-cli`, `kiro-cli`, `pi` | | `PLANNOTATOR_JINA` | `0`/`false` to disable Jina Reader for URL annotation | | `JINA_API_KEY` | Jina Reader API key for higher rate limits | | `PLANNOTATOR_DATA_DIR` | Base directory for Plannotator-managed files (plans, history, drafts, `config.json`). Default: `~/.plannotator`; if that directory doesn't exist and `$XDG_DATA_HOME` is set to an absolute path, `$XDG_DATA_HOME/plannotator` is used instead (also when `~/.plannotator` holds none of Plannotator's data but the XDG folder does). `plannotator data-dir` prints the folder in use | Plannotator-managed files live under `~/.plannotator` by default. Some UI preferences are stored in functional browser cookies. To relocate the files (for example, for an XDG-clean home): ```bash export PLANNOTATOR_DATA_DIR=~/.local/share/plannotator ``` --- ## Development ```bash bun install bun run dev:hook # Plan review server bun run dev:review # Code review editor bun run dev:marketing # Marketing site (plannotator.ai) bun run dev:vscode # VS Code extension (watch mode) ``` ### Build ```bash bun run build # Main targets (hook + opencode + dsh) bun run build:hook # Single-file HTML for the hook server bun run build:review # Code review editor bun run build:opencode # OpenCode plugin bun run build:dsh # DeepSeek Harness plugin bun run build:vscode # VS Code extension ``` Build order matters. The hook build copies pre-built HTML from `apps/review/dist/`. If you change UI code in `packages/ui/`, `packages/editor/`, or `packages/review-editor/`, rebuild the review app first: ```bash bun run --cwd apps/review build && bun run build:hook ``` Test the plugin locally: ```bash claude --plugin-dir ./apps/hook ``` Full binary build: ```bash bun run --cwd apps/review build && bun run build:hook && \ bun build apps/hook/server/index.ts --compile --outfile ~/.local/bin/plannotator ``` --- ## License Copyright 2025-2026 backnotprop Dual-licensed under [Apache 2.0](LICENSE-APACHE) or [MIT](LICENSE-MIT) at your option. Contributions are dual-licensed under the same terms unless you explicitly state otherwise.

# Veyra

作者主页 / Creator： X · @likely2002  |  YouTube · @Likely7Ai

视频教程 / Video tutorials： English · YouTube  |  中文 · 哔哩哔哩

### Real-time GPU Video Enhancement for Windows **Super Resolution · Denoising · HDR · Frame Generation · Capture · PS5 / Xbox / PC Streaming** Turn local video, capture cards and game streaming into one real-time GPU enhancement pipeline.


[![GitHub Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/Likely7/Veyra-NRVideo?style=for-the-badge&logo=github&label=Stars)](https://github.com/Likely7/Veyra-NRVideo/stargazers) [![GitHub Forks](https://img.shields.io/github/forks/Likely7/Veyra-NRVideo?style=for-the-badge&logo=github&label=Forks)](https://github.com/Likely7/Veyra-NRVideo/network/members) [![Latest Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/Likely7/Veyra-NRVideo?style=for-the-badge&logo=github&label=Release)](https://github.com/Likely7/Veyra-NRVideo/releases/latest) [![Release Asset Downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/Likely7/Veyra-NRVideo/total?style=for-the-badge&logo=github&label=Release%20Downloads)](https://github.com/Likely7/Veyra-NRVideo/releases) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/Likely7/Veyra-NRVideo?style=for-the-badge&label=License)](LICENSE)
